summary: Karen C. Lang specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied at Banaras Hindu University, the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, and the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg, later serving as faculty at the University of Virginia.

Karen Katsumoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Her academic posts include serving as a part-time lecturer at Hanazono University (attested 2006) and as a lecturer at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).

Karen McCarthy Brown was a scholar of religious studies and anthropology. Educated at Smith College, Union Theological Seminary, and Temple University, she served as a professor of anthropology at Drew University from circa 1976 to 2009.
Karen Nelson Villanueva is a scholar of religious studies. She earned her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies and studied under the traditional teacher Geshe Ngawang Dakpa.
Karen Nero is a scholar who held academic posts at the University of Canterbury (circa 1998–2004) and the University of Otago.

Karen O'Brien-Kop works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. After completing her PhD at SOAS University of London, she held teaching posts at SOAS, the University of Roehampton (attested 2020), and King's College London (attested 2026).

Karin Meyers works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Jay L. Garfield and served at Kathmandu University as an assistant professor and director of the MA program in Buddhist studies at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Karin Preisendanz specializes in Indology and philosophy. She completed her doctorate and habilitation at the University of Hamburg. Her career includes posts at Freie Universität Berlin, the University of British Columbia, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Vienna.

Karl Albert Agathon Benary was a linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, and under Franz Bopp. He held posts at the Köllnisches Gymnasium, Köllnisches Realgymnasium, and Humboldt University of Berlin.

Karl Ammer was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Vienna from circa 1930 to 1934 and later served as a professor and Director of the Institute of Indology at the University of Halle.

Karl Benedikt Hase worked in linguistics and related fields. Educated at the universities of Jena and Helmstedt, he held positions at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, and the Faculty of Arts of Paris.

Karl Brugmann was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Georg Curtius at the University of Leipzig. He held academic posts at Leipzig, the Russian Institute of Classical Philology, and the University of Freiburg.

Karl Brunnhölzl is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, Tenga Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, the 10th Sangye Nyenpa Rinpoche, Ringu Tulku, and Khenpo Lama Thubten.

Karl Debreczeny is a scholar of Tibetology and art history. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Hung Wu and Jenny Purtle, and served as a curator at the Rubin Museum of Art.

Karl Eduard Zachariae von Lingenthal worked in history and archaeology. He studied at the universities of Leipzig, Berlin, and Heidelberg, and later held a post at Heidelberg University from circa 1836 to 1845.
Karl Eugen Neumann was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Leipzig and earned his doctorate under Richard Pischel.
Karl Felix Halm was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. From circa 1856 to 1882, he held posts at the University of Munich and the Bavarian State Library.

Karl Ferdinand Johansson was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Uppsala University, where he later served as University Professor of Sanskrit and the Comparative Philology of the Indo-European Languages from circa 1893 to 1925.

Karl Florenz specialized in Japanology, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at Leipzig and Berlin under Ernst Windisch, Georg von der Gabelentz, and Friedrich Max Müller, he held posts at the University of Tokyo, Hamburgisches Kolonialinstitut, and the University of Hamburg.

Karl Friedrich Geldner was an Indologist, Iranist, and linguist. He studied at Leipzig and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, later holding academic posts at the University of Tübingen, University of Halle, Humboldt University of Berlin, and University of Marburg.
